newsitem.title: GERMANY: Dresdner says had good start in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Dresdner says had good start in 1997.

text.p: Dresdner Bank AG said on Thursday it had a good start to 1997 with net commission income up significantly and net interest income also up compared with year-earlier levels.

Dresdner Bank chief executive Juergen Sarrazin told the bank's annual news conference that own-account trading income in the first two months matched the disproportionately high level reached in the year-earlier period.
"Dresdner Bank had a good start," Sarrazin said. He said earnings in the first two months were boosted by special factors and could not be extrapolated into a full-year forecast.
Net interest income had been boosted by income relating to trading activities which may not be repeated during the course of the year.
Sarrazin also said risk provisions in 1997 would continue to be burdened by the large number of corporate insolvencies. "We expect risk quotas to remain unchanged," Sarrazin said.
Sarrazin also said Dresdner was able to realise price gains from securities held in its liquidity portfolio in the first two months of 1997, especially from sales of bonds.
"This laid a solid foundation for the rest of the year," Sarrazin said.

Personnel costs rose year-on-year and Dresdner had also budgeted for a disproportionately high rise in non-labour costs since considerable investment is still needed to strengthen the bank's competitive position and secure its earnings potential in the long term, Sarrazin said.
"The business environment will remain difficult for German banks in 1997," Sarrazin said.

"Competition and the trend towards higher interest on deposits will keep the interest rate margin under pressure. On the other hand the good state of the capital markets should continue to benefit commision income business from securities."
Sarrazin predicted that the 1997 result "will enable the bank both to pay an appropriate dividend and continue strengthening reserves."
